System software — runs the computer itself (OS, drivers) vs Application software — does user tasks (MS Word, browsers).
Freeware = free to use; Shareware = free trial, paid after; Open Source = source code publicly editable (e.g. Linux).

questions.q: What is datum in Database Management System?
questions.theory:
DBMS = software to create/manage databases (MySQL, Oracle). RDBMS = DBMS where data is stored in related tables.
ACID properties (transaction reliability): Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
Primary Key = uniquely identifies a row; Foreign Key = links to another table's primary key.
Normalization = organizing tables to reduce data redundancy (Normal Forms: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF...).

questions.q: What is the full-form of TCP? TCP
questions.theory:
Network types by size:
• PAN (Personal Area Network) — few meters, e.g. Bluetooth between phone-earbuds
• LAN (Local Area Network) — one building/campus, e.g. office network
• MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) — one city, links multiple LANs
• WAN (Wide Area Network) — country/global, e.g. the Internet itself
Topologies: Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh, Tree, Hybrid
Key devices: Router (connects networks), Switch (connects devices in one LAN), Modem (digital↔analog for phone/cable line), Gateway (connects different protocol networks)
Key protocols: TCP/IP (core internet), HTTP/HTTPS (web), FTP (file transfer), DNS (name→IP), DHCP (auto-assigns IP)
OSI model (7 layers, top→bottom): Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true about MS Excel?
questions.theory:
Workbook = the whole file; Worksheet = one tab/sheet inside it; Cell = one box (e.g. A1).
Key functions: SUM/AutoSum (adds a range), AVERAGE, CONCATENATE (joins text from cells), VLOOKUP (searches a table)
Every formula starts with =. Cell references: A1 (relative), $A$1 (absolute).

questions.q: Which among the following act as an interface between computer hardware and user?
questions.theory:
Core components: CPU (processes instructions — has ALU+Control Unit+Registers), RAM (volatile, temporary working memory), ROM (non-volatile, stores BIOS/firmware), Motherboard (connects everything)
Memory hierarchy: Registers → Cache → RAM (primary) → Hard Disk/SSD (secondary, permanent storage)
Input devices: keyboard, mouse, scanner, mic | Output devices: monitor, printer, speaker
Power: SMPS converts AC→DC for internal parts; UPS gives backup power during outage
